verdict: No blocking finding for the narrow serialized process cleanup change. Offline review only; no live preflight success claim.
scope: Read-only diff/test inspection, nine new targeted tests, exact three-process deadline/cancellation probe, and one requested normal-completion-gap probe. No source edits/install/models/network/commits.

original_probe_rerun.result: All three have one successful killpg, original TimeoutExpired, no callback error.

normal_completion_gap_probe.result: Cancellation invoked after real communicate returned but before wrapper returned to RunContext. First killpg returned ESRCH, already caught; no callback error; caller CancelledError. No concrete remaining EPERM reproduced.
normal_completion_gap_probe.limitation: Single controlled local probe does not establish every platform/timing outcome. No returncode-only shortcut was requested or introduced.

review_findings.result: Lock serializes finished/stopped checks and group signal. stopped is set only after success or ESRCH. Competing timeout/cancellation paths cannot issue a second successful group signal while drain is pending.
No process.poll/returncode shortcut. Reaped-leader regression verifies descendant holding stdout pipe is still killed and drain completes; unrelated owned-by-test group survives.

PermissionError is not caught or relabeled as success. Genuine first group EPERM is tested both at timeout caller and cancellation callback; callback remains visible through Future logging. Existing limitation of callback exception ownership remains explicit.
Lock covers state and one OS signal; it is not held during process.wait/communicate drain. finished is set under same lock. No new waits, retry allowance, model choice or budget changes.
Only archive.py process cleanup plus new tests changes. No task/site/model-selected behavior, truncation, field projection, refiner schema/accounting or evaluator changes.

limitations: The original failed Codex attempt lacks a full exception stack; this review does not retroactively establish its precise EPERM throw order.
No blanket EPERM suppression is added. An actual first cleanup permission failure remains a failure and may prevent successful drain.
Parent owns broader installed/full-suite verification and fresh live preflight; they are not claimed here.
